# OSHA Arc Flash Safety Training (NFPA 70E 2027)

> 2-hour online course that familiarizes workers with arc flash hazards and the safe work practices in OSHA electrical standards 29 CFR 1910 Subpart S and 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K and the 2027 edition of NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace). Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Regulations: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart S (general industry), 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K (construction), NFPA 70E 2027
- Duration: about 2 hours; 4 lessons plus final exam
- Credits: 0.2 CEU
- Price: $49.99 per person online; bulk pricing from 2 seats
- Other formats: SCORM, virtual instructor-led, in-person
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7, any device; English and Spanish
- Completion window: 3 months; 1 year of access to materials
- Certificate: instant PDF on passing, valid 36 months; renew by retaking every 3 years
- Prerequisites: none

## Definitions
- Arc flash: electric current leaving its intended path and traveling through the air between conductors or to ground, releasing intense heat and light that can cause severe burns or death.
- Arc flash study: an engineering analysis that calculates incident energy, sets protection boundaries, and identifies required PPE and labels.
- OSHA vs NFPA 70E: OSHA is the law (performance-based); NFPA 70E is the consensus standard OSHA looks to for how to comply.

## Who it is for
Electricians; maintenance and facility staff near energized equipment; managers and supervisors of electrical work; equipment operators; janitorial staff with electrical room access; contractors and temporary workers.

## Lessons
1. What is an Arc Flash?
2. Regulatory Overview
3. Controlling Arc Flash Hazards (insulation, guarding, grounding, GFCIs)
4. Arc Flash PPE and Labels
